findings.title: View-only group permission authorizes group creation and moves
findings.body: canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() uses requireManage(), which delegates to this method, so an administrator granted only view permission can create top-level groups or move existing subgroups to the top level by supplying their IDs. Only the MANAGE scope should satisfy this check; add a negative test for an administrator with only all-groups VIEW permission.

findings.title: Return model group IDs rather than authorization resource IDs
findings.body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() passes groupResource.getId() to a helper that looks up resources by their model group ID/name, and then adds that authorization resource ID to the returned set. Authorization resources have independently generated IDs; their names hold the actual group IDs. UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource use this set to restrict user searches by group membership, and user counts also consume it. For example, an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS grant causes the Groups authorization resource's ID to be returned as a group filter, so searches and counts return no members even though direct user access is authorized. Evaluate the correct resource and return actual model group IDs, including handling an all-groups member grant across real groups.

findings.title: Initialize the new resources and scopes for existing permission clients
findings.body: The Groups resource type introduces new scopes and an all-groups resource, but init() immediately returns whenever the realm already has an admin-permissions client. Consequently, a realm initialized before this change never receives manage-membership, manage-members, view-members, or the Groups resource. Creating group permissions with these scopes fails with "No scopes found", and group evaluation can dereference a null all-groups resource. Update existing permission clients idempotently or provide a migration for the newly added schema entries.
